messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content: Analysis reveals an archaic spelling and syntax: “thou” and “myne” suggest early modern or Middle English style, “condicyon” means condition, “fader” father, “hym” him, “strycken” struck, “wyth” with, “destytute” destitute, “wrastle” wrestle, “infirmitie” infirmity, “penurye” penury, “poure” power, “rendre” render, “latter yeeres” later years, “fylled” filled. The sentence is a rhetorical plea: the speaker asks whether he should abandon his blind, poor father when he has the power to provide comfort and joy, implying that such abandonment would be morally wrong. Analysis
